functionality.rationale: False negatives permit overlapping work or stale delivery, while false positives unnecessarily serialize independent tasks.

security.rationale: A stale task could review under obsolete governance or overwrite a security-sensitive fix in an overlapping path.

performance.rationale: Claim, review, and integration add bounded record and Git diff scans over the tracked task catalogue.

compatibility.rationale: Existing schema versions, non-overlapping tasks, custom base refs, and archived task records must retain their legal workflows.

concurrency.rationale: Two simultaneous claims must not both pass an overlap check, and an interrupted claimant must not leave a permanent scheduler lock.

platform.rationale: Pattern matching, Git ancestry, and lock recovery must behave consistently on supported development hosts.

persistence.rationale: Claim locks live in the common Git directory and must recover after process termination without entering tracked history.

adr.rationale: Active ownership and stale-base policy are cross-workstream scheduler contracts.

architecture.rationale: The task changes scheduler governance, not product runtime module boundaries.

roadmap.rationale: Conflict prevention is repository governance rather than a product milestone.
